question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Before proposing your ideas, list in the obvious field the 10 ideas that most experts would propose first for this question (one line each). Then propose your 5 ideas: none of them may be one of the obvious ideas or a minor variant of one. They must still be concrete and scientifically sound.

ideas.title: Heterokaryon fusion to separate cis-chromatin memory from trans-acting AP-1 protein
ideas.description: Fuse a 'primed' cell (prior transient stimulus) with a genetically distinguishable naive cell and use allele-specific ATAC-seq/RNA-seq to ask whether the primed chromatin state is maintained only on the experienced genome or is imposed in trans on the naive genome by the shared AP-1 protein pool. Cis-restricted persistence argues for a chromatin-encoded memory, whereas dominant trans conversion argues that AP-1 is simply a long-lived diffusible signal rather than a memory element.

ideas.title: Quantitative accounting of AP-1 protein lifetime versus memory lifetime
ideas.description: Use HaloTag pulse-chase labeling (plus SILAC turnover measurement) of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN to directly measure degradation and mitotic dilution rates of the AP-1 protein molecules present at the time of stimulation, and compare those decay kinetics quantitatively to the decay of the primed phenotype in the same cells. Memory that substantially outlives the original protein pool, with no sustained new synthesis, cannot be explained by slow TF decay and requires a self-propagating mechanism.

ideas.title: Decoupling the AP-1 autoregulatory circuit without removing the protein
ideas.description: Place JUN/FOS expression under exogenous doxycycline control at the endogenous locus while deleting the endogenous AP-1-bound autoregulatory enhancers, so that AP-1 protein levels can be clamped independently of feedback. If transient stimulation no longer produces a persistent state despite identical AP-1 protein levels, memory is a property of the self-reinforcing circuit rather than of AP-1 occupancy per se.

ideas.title: Synthetic minimal AP-1 memory element
ideas.description: Integrate synthetic arrays of TRE/AP-1 motifs (varying motif number, spacing, flanking nucleosome-positioning sequences, and partner motifs such as TEAD or ETS) upstream of an inert reporter at a defined safe-harbor locus, then deliver a transient AP-1 pulse and measure how long accessibility and reporter expression persist. This reconstitution asks whether AP-1 binding sites alone are sufficient to convert a transient input into a stable state, and defines the minimal sequence grammar required.

ideas.title: Multi-stimulus history decoding to test what information AP-1 actually stores
ideas.description: Expose cells to ordered combinations of distinct AP-1-activating inputs (e.g., growth factor, mechanical stretch, cytokine) in different sequences and intervals, then train a classifier on single-cell AP-1 binding/accessibility profiles to decode which history a cell experienced, quantifying mutual information between past input and present state as a function of elapsed time and divisions. A genuine memory mechanism should preserve stimulus identity and order rather than collapsing all histories onto a single magnitude axis.

obvious: ATAC-seq time course after transient stimulation to find persistent AP-1-motif-enriched accessible regions
FOS/JUN ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN time course testing for persistent genomic occupancy after signal decay
Prime-rest-restimulate protocols measuring faster or stronger secondary transcriptional responses
Knockdown/knockout of Fos/Jun family members or A-Fos dominant negative during the rest window to erase memory
Inducible or optogenetic AP-1 expression to test sufficiency for installing the primed state
CRISPR deletion or point mutation of AP-1 motifs in candidate memory enhancers
Histone modification profiling (H3K4me1/H3K27ac) at AP-1 sites to detect latent enhancer priming
Single-cell multiome (RNA + ATAC) linking AP-1 chromatin state to subsequent fate choice
Clonal barcoding/lineage tracing to test heritability of AP-1-high states across divisions
Live-cell AP-1 reporter imaging correlating prior signaling dynamics with later phenotype
